log.text: Floette used Light of Ruin → Gengar

decisions.rationale: Lead Gengar-Mega + Excadrill per plan: Gengar Mega Evolves turn 1 for Shadow Tag (traps Floette if present) and Taunts Scrafty to block Snarl/Fake Out disruption. Excadrill Focus Sash guarantees survival; at 154 Speed it outspeeds Scrafty/Milotic/Metagross and can Rock Slide (SE on Garchomp/Talonflame) or High Horsepower Scrafty. Backline Tyranitar provides Sand Stream for Excadrill's Sand Rush when switched in, plus Rock Slide spread pressure. Gholdengo is the late-game cleaner: Make It Rain is SE on Floette-Fairy, but must stay benched until Scrafty is removed to avoid Snarl + self-drop compounding to -6 SpA.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 lead: Gengar-Mega + Excadrill, back Tyranitar + Gholdengo. Plan: (1) Gengar Taunt on Scrafty turn 1 if present — blocks Snarl and Fake Out follow-up. (2) Excadrill Focus Sash guarantees one action; prioritize High Horsepower on Scrafty to remove it before Gholdengo enters. (3) If Floette leads unevolved, Shadow Tag traps it turn 1 after Mega Evo; target with Shadow Ball/Sludge Bomb for KO before Fairy Aura Light of Ruin escalates. (4) Bring Tyranitar in when Excadrill needs Sand Rush (308 Speed); Tyranitar also spreads Rock Slide. (5) Gholdengo only enters after Scrafty is dead — Make It Rain SE on Floette, but Snarl + self-SpA-drop is catastrophic. (6) Do NOT use stat-lowering moves on Milotic (Competitive +2 SpA); Taunt shuts its Recover/Protect. (7) Watch for Talonflame Gale Wings Brave Bird priority and Metagross Bullet Punch priority — both unplayed through 2 games, expected game 3. (8) Excadrill Rock Slide is 4x SE on Talonflame and SE on Garchomp; High Horsepower is neutral but high-power on Scrafty. (9) Scrafty Roseli Berry intact — first SE Fairy hit weakened (relevant if Spirit Break or Moonblast targeted).

decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Floette plus Scrafty to pressure Tyranitar, Tauros, and Mega Gengar while giving immediate Snarl control into the Gengar/Gholdengo core. Garchomp supplies crucial Ground pressure into both Steel-types, and Talonflame provides Tailwind, Taunt, and Fire coverage for Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Mega Gengar revealed Taunt, Shadow Ball, and Protect. Gholdengo revealed Leftovers, Protect, Recover, Shadow Ball, and Make It Rain. Snarl is valuable into their special core despite Good as Gold. Prioritize Scrafty plus Mega Floette versus Gengar/Gholdengo, with Garchomp or Talonflame retained for Gholdengo pressure.

decisions.rationale: Mega Gengar SpA 222 Sludge Bomb is 2x SE STAB on Floette, estimated ~70-123% with Mega stats — very likely OHKO removing the Light of Ruin threat. Gengar Speed 200 outspeeds both foes so Sludge Bomb resolves before any Snarl. Excadrill Protects to block Scrafty's Fake Out (priority +3, targets Excadrill since Gengar is Ghost-immune), preserving Focus Sash and 100% HP. Shadow Tag traps both non-Ghost opponents for future cleanup. If Floette survives, Excadrill finishes next turn with Iron Head; if KO'd, pivot to Taunt+High Horsepower on trapped Scrafty.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 lead: Gengar-Mega + Excadrill vs Floette-Eternal + Scrafty. Mega Gengar confirmed stats: HP137/Atk76/Def100/SpA222/SpD115/Spe200. Sludge Bomb on Floette estimated ~70-123% (likely OHKO with Mega SpA 222). Floette Light of Ruin on Gengar ~44-64% (NVE). Plan turn 2: if Floette KO'd, Gengar Taunt Scrafty (blocks Snarl/Protect 3 turns) + Excadrill High Horsepower Scrafty (trapped by Shadow Tag, can't Protect). If Floette survives low, Excadrill Iron Head finishes. Scrafty Fake Out only usable turn 1. Do NOT let Scrafty Snarl stack on Gengar SpA — Taunt by turn 2 at latest. Back: Tyranitar (Sand Rush Excadrill=308 Spe, Rock Slide spread) + Gholdengo (enter only after Scrafty dead; Make It Rain SE on Floette). Watch for Talonflame Gale Wings BB priority and Metagross Bullet Punch priority from unrevealed back Pokémon.

selection: Light of Ruin -> foe 1 (Gengar) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Mega Light of Ruin maximizes immediate pressure on Gengar while Fake Out prevents Excadrill's Iron Head and preserves Floette's attack.
decisions.notebook: Mega Floette is Fairy Aura with base 155 SpA, 148 SpD, and 102 Speed; Timid raw Speed reaches 169. Floettite enables Mega Evolution for Eternal Flower Floette.

decisions.rationale: Preserve Garchomp’s endgame pressure while Talonflame can establish priority Tailwind from full HP and immediately threatens the weakened Mega Gengar with Gale Wings Brave Bird next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mega Gengar is Timid with Shadow Tag, Sludge Bomb, Shadow Ball, Taunt, and Protect; its raw Speed range is 165-200. Opponent Excadrill is Jolly Sand Rush with Focus Sash, Iron Head, High Horsepower, Rock Slide, and Protect. Garchomp Life Orb Earthquake always KOs Mega Gengar from 24% and can OHKO Excadrill, but is spread damage and also damages its ally. Talonflame’s full-HP Gale Wings grants +1 priority to Tailwind and Brave Bird; Brave Bird KOs Mega Gengar from 24%.

decisions.rationale: Gengar at 25% is guaranteed KO'd by Talonflame's Gale Wings Brave Bird (priority +1, 50-79% of max HP). Protect (priority +4) is the only way to survive and maintain Shadow Tag. Excadrill Rock Slide chunks Talonflame to 11-52% (removing Gale Wings for next turn since no longer full HP) while hitting Scrafty for chip. Next turn: Gengar outspeeds Talonflame (200 vs 160-195 without Gale Wings priority) to Taunt Scrafty, Excadrill finishes Talonflame. If Talonflame Tailwinds instead, Rock Slide still chunks it and Gengar can Protect again next turn while Excadrill KOs the weakened Talonflame.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 turn 2: Floette KO'd turn 1, Talonflame in. Brave Bird w/ Gale Wings priority guaranteed KO on 25% Gengar — must Protect. Rock Slide chunks Talonflame to 11-52% (removes Gale Wings next turn). Plan turn 3: Gengar Taunt Scrafty + Excadrill finish Talonflame. Scrafty trapped by Shadow Tag, Fake Out already used. Back: Tyranitar (Sand Rush Excadrill=308 Spe) + Gholdengo. Watch for 4th unrevealed foe — Garchomp/Milotic/Metagross. If Gengar falls later, Shadow Tag breaks and foe can switch — prioritize keeping Gengar alive to maintain trap.

decisions.rationale: Use Gale Wings Brave Bird to guarantee Mega Gengar’s KO unless it Protects, while Drain Punch makes progress on Excadrill through its Focus Sash.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar is Timid Shadow Tag with Sludge Bomb, Shadow Ball, Taunt, and Protect. Excadrill is Jolly Sand Rush with Focus Sash, Iron Head, High Horsepower, Rock Slide, and Protect. Garchomp Life Orb Earthquake always KOs low Mega Gengar and can OHKO Excadrill, but damages its ally. Full-HP Talonflame has +1 priority on Tailwind and Brave Bird; Brave Bird guarantees a KO on Mega Gengar from 24%.

decisions.rationale: Gengar outspeeds and guaranteed-KOs Talonflame with Sludge Bomb before it can act, preserving Gengar at 25%. Switching Excadrill to Gholdengo is strictly optimal: Gholdengo is immune to Scrafty's Drain Punch (Ghost typing), tanks Snarl for only 12-23%, and if Scrafty targeted Excadrill's slot with Drain Punch the move fails entirely. This preserves Excadrill on bench for later Sand Rush with Tyranitar while bringing in a fresh Gholdengo. Shadow Tag maintained if Gengar survives Snarl (~50% chance); even if Gengar falls, Gholdengo at ~85% HP is a strong position with Tyranitar in back.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Floette KO'd turn 1. Talonflame at 27% KO'd turn 3 by Gengar Sludge Bomb. Excadrill switched to Gholdengo turn 3 to avoid guaranteed Drain Punch KO and exploit Gholdengo's Fighting immunity. Scrafty trapped by Shadow Tag while Gengar lives. Opponent 4th Pokémon unrevealed: Garchomp/Milotic/Metagross. Backline: Tyranitar (Sand Stream → Excadrill Sand Rush 308 Spe) + Excadrill at 32% on bench. If Gengar survives, maintain Shadow Tag trap on Scrafty. If Gengar falls, Shadow Tag breaks and opponent can switch — prioritize bringing Tyranitar for sand + Excadrill speed control. Gholdengo immune to Drain Punch; use as Scrafty counter.

decisions.rationale: Flare Blitz guarantees Excadrill’s removal before it can act if Talonflame survives Gengar’s attack, while Snarl pressures Mega Gengar and lowers its Special Attack for the ensuing endgame. This line remains useful even if Gengar moves first or Protects.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar is Timid Shadow Tag with Sludge Bomb, Shadow Ball, Taunt, and Protect. Excadrill is Jolly Sand Rush with Focus Sash, Iron Head, High Horsepower, Rock Slide, and Protect. Garchomp Life Orb Earthquake can KO Mega Gengar and Excadrill but damages its ally. Full-HP Talonflame gets Gale Wings priority on Tailwind and Brave Bird; Brave Bird KOs Mega Gengar from low HP.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Opponent has only Garchomp + Scrafty left (no switches), so Shadow Tag is worthless — sacrifice Gengar's slot to bring Tyranitar (100% HP, survives EQ at 61-87%, sets Sand for Excadrill's 308 Spe). Gholdengo Protects because Garchomp Earthquake does 72-105% to it (possible OHKO). Preserve the 3v2 advantage and set up sand for Excadrill cleanup next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent brought Garchomp/Scrafty/Floette/Talonflame only — Floette and Talonflame fainted, so opponent has ONLY Garchomp + Scrafty remaining (no bench). We have 3v2 advantage. Plan: Tyranitar sets sand → switch to Excadrill (Sand Rush 308 Spe) to outspeed and KO Garchomp with High Horsepower. Gholdengo is the Scrafty answer (immune to Drain Punch/Fake Out, only fears Snarl 2x). Excadrill Focus Sash already consumed (took Drain Punch turn 2, now at 32%). Tyranitar Ice Punch is 4x on Garchomp but Tyranitar is too slow (81 Spe) to outspeed Garchomp (134-169) — must use Excadrill sand rush instead. Key damage refs: Garchomp EQ does 61-87% to Tyranitar, 72-105% to Gholdengo; Gholdengo Shadow Ball does 31-57% to Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Earthquake plus Snarl guarantees Mega Gengar is removed if it does not Protect, while giving the best immediate chance to KO Gholdengo; Scrafty survives the allied Earthquake and Snarl provides useful Special Attack control afterward.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp Life Orb Earthquake guarantees the low-HP Mega Gengar KO and has a possible OHKO range on full-HP Gholdengo, while dealing roughly half to allied Scrafty. Scrafty's Snarl guarantees a KO on Mega Gengar at 5% and is weak chip into Gholdengo.

decisions.rationale: Tyranitar Protects (first use, reliable) to survive at 12%. Gholdengo Make It Rain chunks both foes: 35-64% on Garchomp (to 26-55%), 33-59% on Scrafty (possible KO from 50%). If opponent Earthquakes, Scrafty takes 30-64% collateral + Make It Rain = guaranteed faint, leaving 3v1 — but Gholdengo risks OHKO (72-105%). However, Earthquake is a losing play for the opponent (loses Scrafty), so they likely use NVE Dragon Claw/Rock Slide on Gholdengo instead, keeping it safe. Next turn: switch Tyranitar→Excadrill (Sand Rush 308 Spe) to outspeed and finish chunked Garchomp. Ice Punch was rejected because Tyranitar (81 Spe) is outsped by Garchomp (134-169) and likely by Scrafty (78-110), dying before it can attack.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 key damage refs: Garchomp EQ collateral on Scrafty = 30-64% (at 50% HP, EQ+Make It Rain always KOs Scrafty). Gholdengo Make It Rain: 35-64% on Garchomp, 33-59% on Scrafty. Garchomp EQ on Gholdengo = 72-105% (possible OHKO). Tyranitar Ice Punch on Garchomp = 73-131% (possible KO from 90% but Tyranitar too slow to execute). Excadrill at 32% HP dies to Garchomp EQ (neutral ~50-70% of max HP > 32% remaining). Plan: Protect Tyranitar, Make It Rain to chunk foes, then bring Excadrill next turn under Sand Rush to finish Garchomp. Opponent has only Garchomp+Scrafty remaining (no bench).

decisions.rationale: Excadrill under Sand Rush outspeeds both foes and is the only Pokémon with a winning path: Rock Slide flinch chance on Garchomp (30%) lets Tyranitar survive to Ice Punch (4x SE) for the KO, then Iron Head (2x SE) cleans up Scrafty. Gengar-Mega at 6% dies to Sandstorm chip and has no SE moves or bench to trap with Shadow Tag. Not forfeiting because this is decisive game 3 and the flinch line gives a real, if slim, win chance.
decisions.notebook: Series tied 1-1, game 3 decisive. Opponent team: Garchomp (Jolly, Life Orb, Rough Skin, EQ/Rock Slide/Dragon Claw/Protect), Scrafty (Careful, Roseli Berry, Intimidate, Fake Out/Snarl/Drain Punch/Protect), Floette-Mega (Timid, Floettite, Fairy Aura), Talonflame (Jolly, Focus Sash, Gale Wings), Milotic (Bold, Leftovers, Competitive), Metagross (Adamant, Lum Berry, Clear Body). Key speed tiers: Garchomp 134-169, Scrafty 78-110, Talonflame 160-195 (Gale Wings priority BB). Excadrill Sand Rush outspeeds all. Garchomp EQ collateral on Scrafty = 30-64%. Tyranitar Ice Punch on Garchomp = 73-131% (4x SE).

decisions.rationale: Earthquake guarantees Tyranitar’s KO while retaining a possible immediate KO on Gholdengo; Protect prevents allied Earthquake damage and covers Make It Rain.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp’s Life Orb Earthquake is the primary way to pressure or potentially remove Gholdengo while also punishing Tyranitar and Excadrill. Preserve Scrafty with Protect when using allied Earthquake if its utility remains valuable.

decisions.rationale: Both attacks target Garchomp for a guaranteed KO (Iron Head 27-48% + Ice Punch 72.6-131% = 99.6% min > 80% HP). Iron Head's 20% flinch chance is the only defense against Garchomp's Earthquake which would KO both my Pokemon. If Garchomp doesn't EQ (flinch, Protect prediction, or Scrafty collateral concern), both hits land and Garchomp is eliminated, leaving Excadrill + Tyranitar vs Scrafty alone which is winnable. High Horsepower offers no flinch protection and lower accuracy.
decisions.notebook: Series tied 1-1, game 3 decisive. Opponent team fully scouted: Garchomp (Jolly LO Rough Skin 134-169 Spe), Scrafty (Careful Roseli Intimidate 78-110 Spe), Floette-Mega (Timid Floettite Fairy Aura fainted), Talonflame (Jolly Sash Gale Wings fainted), Milotic (Bold Leftovers Competitive not brought), Metagross (Adamant Lum ClearBody not brought). Excadrill Sand Rush 308 outspeeds all. Tyranitar Ice Punch 4x SE on Garchomp = 72.6-131% of max. Iron Head 20% flinch (not 30%). Garchomp EQ guaranteed KO on both Ttar(12%) and Exca(32%). Scrafty Drain Punch 4x SE on Ttar, 2x SE on Exca, both guaranteed KO. Scrafty speed uncertain vs Ttar (78-110 vs 81).

decisions.rationale: Both Tyranitar and Excadrill are fainted; Gengar-Mega at 6% is my only remaining Pokémon. Sending it out rather than forfeiting because Gengar (Speed 200) outspeeds both foes and Shadow Ball is a guaranteed KO on Garchomp (34.9-62.3% vs 26% HP). After that, Gengar moves first vs Scrafty and Sludge Bomb (36.6-65%) has a real chance to KO from 38%. Slot 1 switches Gengar in; Slot 2 passes since no other Pokémon remain.
decisions.notebook: Series tied 1-1, game 3 decisive. Opponent fully scouted: Garchomp (Jolly LO Rough Skin 134-169 Spe), Scrafty (Careful Roseli Intimidate 78-110 Spe), Floette-Mega (Timid Floettite Fairy Aura fainted), Talonflame (Jolly Sash Gale Wings fainted), Milotic (Bold Leftovers Competitive not brought), Metagross (Adamant Lum ClearBody not brought). Key damage calcs: Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball guaranteed KO on Garchomp at 26% (34.9-62.3% of max). Gengar Sludge Bomb vs Scrafty 36.6-65% of max (possible KO from 38%). Gengar outspeeds both foes (200 vs 134-169 and 78-110). Gengar SpA at -1 from Snarl. Scrafty Protect streak 2 (heavily reduced success). Garchomp Life Orb recoil chips 10% per attack.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Earthquake guarantees both opposing active KOs after Excadrill’s move; Scrafty’s Protect is the only way to preserve it from allied Earthquake for the remaining Mega Gengar endgame.
decisions.notebook: Life Orb Garchomp Earthquake is the central spread-pressure option. Scrafty can preserve itself alongside allied Earthquake with Protect, though consecutive Protect is unreliable.

decisions.rationale: 1v2 with Gengar at 6% — any hit KOs me, but Gengar outspeeds both foes. Shadow Ball is a guaranteed KO on Garchomp (34.9-62.3% at -1 SpA > 26% HP). After that, Scrafty's only KO move is Snarl; Fake Out and Drain Punch are both immune to Ghost, leaving a sliver of hope if the opponent misplays. This strictly maximizes win probability over forfeiting (0%) or targeting Scrafty (Sludge Bomb not guaranteed KO at 36.6% min vs 38%, and Garchomp KO's Gengar with any move).
decisions.notebook: Series tied 1-1, Game 3 decisive. Opponent fully scouted: Garchomp (Jolly LO Rough Skin 134-169 Spe), Scrafty (Careful Roseli Intimidate 78-110 Spe), Floette-Mega (Timid Floettite Fairy Aura), Talonflame (Jolly Sash Gale Wings), Milotic (Bold Leftovers Competitive), Metagross (Adamant Lum ClearBody). Key calcs: Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball guaranteed KO on Garchomp at 26% even at -1 SpA (34.9-62.3%). Gengar Sludge Bomb vs Scrafty 36.6-65% (not guaranteed KO from 38%). Scrafty Fake Out/Drain Punch immune to Ghost; only Snarl damages Gengar. Gengar outspeeds both remaining foes (200 vs 134-169, 78-110).

decisions.rationale: Protect Garchomp while Scrafty uses Snarl; Mega Gengar cannot avoid sandstorm chip at its shown HP, and this prevents a possible Sludge Bomb KO on Garchomp.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Mega Gengar has Shadow Tag and is vulnerable to Ground; Life Orb Garchomp Earthquake remains primary spread pressure, but preserve Garchomp when residual damage can secure the endgame.

reflections.summary: Lost Game 3 and the series because Garchomp's Earthquake devastated an Earthquake-weak core: Tyranitar (4x), Excadrill (2x), and Gholdengo (2x) all fell to Earthquake across turns 5-6 while Scrafty consistently Protected to avoid friendly fire. Gengar was crippled on turn 1 by Floette-Mega's Light of Ruin (75% damage) and then chipped to 6% by Snarl, leaving it unable to finish Garchomp at 26% because Garchomp read the Shadow Ball and Protected on the final turn. The sand core (Tyranitar + Excadrill) was a poor structural fit against a team with Garchomp Earthquake + Scrafty Protect, since both sand members are Ground-weak and Excadrill was already at 32% from Drain Punch before sand was even set. Bringing Grimmsnarl over Tyranitar would have provided Prankster support, a Dark/Dragon resist, and no Ground weakness. The Mega Gengar choice was reasonable for trapping and Sludge Bomb did remove Floette via recoil, but the overall four brought were too Earthquake-fragile.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent in a future series, do not bring two or more Earthquake-weak Pokemon alongside each other when Garchomp + Scrafty Protect is a known combination. Replace Tyranitar with Grimmsnarl (Prankster screens/Taunt, resists Snarl and Dragon Claw, immune to Earthquake via typing matchup pressure) or Paldean Tauros Aqua (Intimidate to cut Garchomp's Attack, Water STAB for Garchomp). Keep Mega Gengar for trapping but preserve its HP better—avoid tanking Light of Ruin if possible, since Gengar at low HP cannot clean up late game.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: leads with Fake Out Scrafty + Mega Floette, prioritizes early aggression with Light of Ruin. Scrafty is Careful Roseli Intimidate with Snarl spam, Drain Punch, and well-timed Protect—reads Protect patterns accurately. Garchomp is Jolly Life Orb Rough Skin with Earthquake as the primary win condition; opponent protects Scrafty from friendly EQ while sweeping with Garchomp. Floette-Mega is Timid Fairy Aura with Light of Ruin (massive recoil—can self-KO at low HP). Talonflame is Jolly Sash Gale Wings, used as fast Brave Bird pressure. Milotic (Bold Leftovers Competitive) and Metagross (Adamant Lum ClearBody) were not brought in Game 3. Key prep conclusions: avoid Ground-weak cores against this team; Grimmsnarl is a strong bring for Prankster utility and Dark/Dragon resists; Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball KOs Garchomp at 26% even at -1 SpA but must survive to act; opponent Protect-reads well, so mix up timing. Scrafty Roseli Berry means Fairy moves won't KO it from mid-range.

reflections.summary: Won game 3 and the series 2-1 because the Gengar/Excadrill lead was pressured into defensive lines while Mega Floette's sacrifice left Mega Gengar at 24%, allowing Scrafty Snarl to reduce it to 5%. Talonflame then absorbed the key attacks, and the Garchomp/Scrafty endgame converted repeated Earthquake pressure into KOs on Gholdengo, Tyranitar, and Excadrill before Scrafty finished Gengar. The between-game approach helped: Scrafty's Intimidate, repeated Snarl, and Protects gave Life Orb Garchomp the protected turns it needed. Piloting was clean with no recorded errors. At preview, Floette/Scrafty/Talonflame/Garchomp was a suitable four: Floette forced immediate damage into Gengar, Scrafty was crucial utility, Talonflame provided expendable tempo, and Garchomp was the decisive win condition. Mega Floette was a reasonable evolution choice despite being immediately removed; it created the Gengar endgame threshold. For series preparation, the registered six fit well: Garchomp and Scrafty were especially strong into the revealed Steel/sand core, while Floette gave a direct Mega Gengar pressure option. Nothing in the unused roster is evidenced to have been a materially better game-3 alternative; Metagross, Milotic, and the unused seasonal options have no revealed matchup advantage strong enough to displace the winning four.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, retain the Garchomp/Scrafty-centered plan against this opponent's Mega Gengar, Gholdengo, Tyranitar, and Excadrill structure. Respect Excadrill Protect when using Fake Out and avoid relying on Talonflame to survive Rock Slide; treat it primarily as a tempo or sacrifice piece. Preserve Garchomp through the midgame with Scrafty Protect and Intimidate so Earthquake can clean the sand endgame. If Mega Gengar is exposed, prioritize bringing it into Ground- or Snarl-finishing range rather than trying to preserve Floette after it has achieved that damage.
reflections.notebook: Opponent revealed Mega Gengar with Sludge Bomb, Shadow Ball, Taunt, and Protect; it is an important early offensive piece but is vulnerable to Ground pressure and can be finished by Snarl after chip. Gholdengo carries Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Protect, and Recover with Leftovers; Good as Gold prevents status-based disruption, but it is highly vulnerable to Garchomp Earthquake. Tyranitar uses Smooth Rock Sand Stream and has Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, and Protect; its sand enables Jolly Focus Sash Sand Rush Excadrill, which showed Iron Head, High Horsepower, Rock Slide, and Protect. Grimmsnarl and Aqua Tauros were available but not brought in game 3, so screens/Fake Out and Intimidate remain plausible alternate modes. Scrafty is highly valuable into this roster: Intimidate weakens the physical sand core, Snarl checks the special attackers, and Protect creates safe Earthquake turns. Life Orb Garchomp is the central closer versus the revealed Steel/sand composition; preserve it until opposing Protects and sash pressure are managed. Mega Floette can trade for meaningful Mega Gengar chip, but do not expect it to survive a Sludge Bomb. Prep conclusion: the registered roster's Garchomp/Scrafty/Floette/Talonflame mode successfully matched the opponent, with no evidence yet that a full-roster alternative is superior.
